classification.difficultyReason: Compare three junction values, sketch restricted nonlinear branches with endpoint markers, and combine branch ranges while accounting for an isolated function value.

content.prompt: Find whether each function is continuous at $x=2$. Then sketch the curve and state the domain and range.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}f(2)&=2^3=8\\\text{Left branch at }2&=2^3=8\\\text{Right branch at }2&=10-2=8\end{align*}$$Both branches meet at the function value, so $f$ is continuous at $x=2$. The cubic branch covers $y\le8$, and the line adds no larger values. Domain: $\mathbb R$. Range: $(-\infty,8]$.

spec.description: Cubic and line joined at (2,8), with dashed junction guides.
spec.mathematics: y=x^3 for x<=2; y=10-x for x>2.

answer.short: Not continuous at $x=2$: the adjoining branches approach $9$, but $f(2)=4$. Domain: $\mathbb R$. Range: $(-\infty,9)$.
answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}f(2)&=4\\\text{Left branch at }2&=3^2=9\\\text{Right branch at }2&=13-2^2=9\end{align*}$$The neighbouring branches approach $9$, which differs from $f(2)$, so $f$ is not continuous at $x=2$. The right branch takes every value below $9$; the value $4$ is already in that range. Domain: $\mathbb R$. Range: $(-\infty,9)$.

spec.description: Exponential and quadratic branches approach open point (2,9); isolated filled point (2,4). The exact positive intercept is labelled.
spec.mathematics: y=3^x for x<2; y=13-x^2 for x>2; f(2)=4. Positive intercept sqrt(13).

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}f(2)&=\frac12\\\text{Left branch at }2&=\frac12\\\text{Right branch at }2&=1-\frac14(2)=\frac12\end{align*}$$Both branches meet at the function value, so $f$ is continuous at $x=2$. The reciprocal branch gives $y>\tfrac12$, the point at $x=2$ gives $y=\tfrac12$, and the line gives $y<\tfrac12$. Domain: $(0,\infty)$. Range: $\mathbb R$.

spec.description: Reciprocal branch joins the line at (2,1/2); the line crosses at (4,0). The y-axis is the reciprocal branch's vertical asymptote.

answer.short: Not continuous at $x=2$: the left branch approaches $2$ and the right branch approaches $0$. Domain: $\mathbb R$. Range: $(-\infty,2]$.
answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}f(2)&=2\\\text{Left branch at }2&=2\\\text{Right branch at }2&=2-2=0\end{align*}$$The branch values differ, so $f$ is not continuous at $x=2$. The left branch gives every value below $2$, and $f(2)=2$. Domain: $\mathbb R$. Range: $(-\infty,2]$.

spec.description: Rising line ends at filled (2,2); descending ray begins at open (2,0).
spec.mathematics: y=x for x<2; y=2-x for x>2; f(2)=2.
